coolmax.types: COOLMAX is a family of polyester moisture-management technologies licensed to fiber, yarn and fabric makers. The core COOLMAX technology uses polyester fibers with engineered, non-round cross-sections and fine filaments that move liquid sweat by capillary action. COOLMAX EcoMade versions, introduced by The LYCRA Company with ITOCHU in 2021 for the textile-waste route, are made from either 100% recycled PET bottles or 100% pre-consumer textile waste from cutting rooms, the latter processed by depolymerization and refining into polyester with properties the company says match virgin fiber. Different fabric programs are certified for specific constructions, so COOLMAX denotes a tested fabric specification as much as a fiber.
coolmax.fabrics: COOLMAX fabrics are used in running and cycling shirts, sports bras and underwear, socks (often blended with nylon, wool or spandex), workwear, and bedding and mattress covers marketed for cooling. Constructions are typically single jersey, pique and mesh knits, and two-faced knits that pull moisture from the skin side to the outer face. It is often blended with cotton or wool to combine wicking with a softer hand.
coolmax.quality: Check the content label for polyester and any blend fibers, and look for a COOLMAX hangtag or sewn-in label, which licensed fabrics carry. Wicking can be compared using standardized tests such as AATCC TM197 (vertical wicking) and TM195 (liquid moisture management), so ask brands for results. At home, drip water on the inside face: good wicking fabric absorbs and spreads it within seconds. Hydrophilic finishes can wash out, so treat claims of permanence skeptically. Many unbranded 'wicking' polyesters work similarly; the brand indicates a licensed specification, not a unique physics.
pros: Engineered fiber cross-sections move sweat to the fabric surface where it evaporates quickly.
Polyester keeps its strength when wet and dries fast, suiting sport and hot conditions.
EcoMade versions made from recycled bottles or textile waste reduce reliance on virgin polymer, according to the producer.
Licensing and fabric certification give some consistency across mills.
cons: Polyester retains body odor more than wool or cotton, especially in synthetic-only fabrics.
It sheds persistent microfibers, and recycled polyester may shed more than virgin.
Wicking finishes can degrade with washing and fabric softener.
The brand is one of many similar wicking polyesters, so the premium buys certification rather than unique performance.
coolmax.impact: COOLMAX is polyester, so its footprint follows PET production: fossil feedstocks for virgin fiber, or recycled bottles and textile waste for EcoMade versions, which the producer presents as keeping waste out of landfill. The textile-waste route uses chemical depolymerization, which can return polyester to near-virgin quality but requires energy; comparative figures are producer-reported. The main independent concern is microfiber shedding during laundering. A 2024 study in Environmental Pollution (Akyildiz and colleagues) found recycled polyester fabric released more microplastic fibers than virgin polyester under identical 40 C washes (about 1,193 versus 908 fibers counted). Durable, well-constructed knits and cooler, fuller washes reduce shedding over a garment's life.
coolmax.care: Wash inside out at 30 to 40 C with liquid detergent; odor-control or sport detergents help because polyester holds body oils. Never use fabric softener or dryer sheets, which coat fibers and block wicking. Wash soon after use rather than leaving damp gear in a bag. Line dry or tumble on low; high heat can damage spandex blends and set creases. Iron rarely, on a low setting (about 110 C). For stubborn odor, a pre-soak in water with a little white vinegar or an enzyme detergent often helps. A microfiber-catching bag or filter reduces shedding.
faq: Polyester with specially shaped fiber cross-sections and fine filaments that move sweat by capillary action. EcoMade versions use 100% recycled polyester from bottles or pre-consumer textile waste, according to The LYCRA Company.
Is COOLMAX better than merino for running?

They work differently. COOLMAX polyester wicks and dries quickly and is durable, while merino absorbs vapor and resists odor better. For hot, high-sweat activity many prefer wicking polyester; for multi-day wear without washing, merino often wins.
Why does my COOLMAX shirt still smell after washing?

Polyester binds body oils and odor-causing bacteria. Wash soon after use, turn inside out, skip fabric softener, and use a sport or enzyme detergent. An occasional soak with a little white vinegar can help.
notable: The LYCRA Company and ITOCHU introduced COOLMAX EcoMade fiber made from 100% textile waste in 2021, using depolymerization to recover polyester from cutting-room scraps.
COOLMAX's wicking depends on fiber shape: channeled, non-round cross-sections create capillaries that move liquid along the yarn.
